Subject: MAP draft: performance validation checklist & proposed tests

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a working draft of the Mutual Action Plan (acme_map_v3.xlsx) with the evaluation milestones. Key items I want to confirm so we can lock dates into the MAP:

- Evaluation goals: validate latency (p50/p95/p99), TTFT (time-to-first-token), sustained throughput at target concurrency, and queueing/backpressure behavior under sudden bursts.
- Test windows: 11/30–12/04 (baseline + controlled burst probes), with a final verification run 12/07.
- Acceptance criteria (provisional): p95 latency <= 500ms for 2k tokens/sec workload at steady state; TTFT <= 1.5s for cold connections; graceful degradation with exponential backoff and maintained availability >99.5% during burst.
- Deliverables from Redwood: test plan, raw logs (burst_probe_results.csv), SLO proposal (slo_proposal.pdf), and a one-page executive summary.
- Decision milestone: Procurement sign-off + technical acceptance (closed) => targeted contract signature by 12/15.

If this looks good, please confirm so we can schedule the test windows and get your devops on the call for the burst probe. I’ve copied Rishi and Neha to align on the instrumentation and metrics.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: MAP draft: performance validation checklist & proposed tests — technical plan

Sam / Olga —

Below is the technical test plan we’ll execute during the baseline and burst windows. Please review and flag anything we should tune:

1) Baseline (steady-state)
- Target steady throughput: 200 requests/sec (avg), payloads average ~360 tokens per request.
- Duration: 60 minutes warm-up + 120 minutes measurement.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, TTFT, token/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, KV-cache hit rate.

2) Burst probe (short peak tests)
- Ramp pattern: 0 -> 1.5k rps over 30s, hold 60s, decay back to steady over 30s. Repeat 3x with 5m rest.
- Observability: request queue length, enqueue latency, token emission rate, rate-limit triggered counts, error codes.
- Safety: we honor Sam’s ask — max sustained overload 60s; we’ll notify devops 10m before each run.

3) Longer stress (steady overload) — only if baseline meets acceptance
- Ramp to 800 rps sustained for 10m to observe queueing and autoscale behavior.

4) Acceptance verification
- TTFT measured from connection start to first token; must be <1.5s for >95% of requests on baseline.
- p95 token latency under defined throughput target <= 500ms.

Instrumentation notes:
- We’ll produce a CSV (burst_probe_results.csv) with per-request timestamps, queue_length, backend_latency, tokens_emitted.
- We’ll include a distilled runbook recommending rate-limit windows (per-route token/sec) and backpressure thresholds.

Marcus — please run the probe from our east region cluster and paste results into the shared folder. Neha — I’ll need the SLO template for Acme to drop into the MAP.

Thanks,
Rishi
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP draft: performance validation checklist & proposed tests — burst probe results (summary)

Team / Sam —

We completed the baseline and burst probes this morning from us-east. Quick summary (full CSV attached):

Baseline (steady 200 rps, 2.5h run)
- p50 latency: 110ms
- p95 latency: 380ms
- p99 latency: 820ms (rare long tails correlated with cold cache evictions)
- TTFT median: 0.9s; TTFT 95th: 1.3s
- GPU utilization during measurement: 62% avg

Burst probes (3 x 30s ramps to 1.5k rps, 60s hold)
- Observed behavior: request queue length spiked linearly after ~1800 concurrent queued requests; enqueue latency increased and TTFT grew to 2.8–3.6s during hold windows.
- p95 token latency during peak: 1.2s (degraded vs baseline)
- Error surface: <0.2% 429 (rate-limit) and <0.1% 503 (temporary capacity) across runs.
- Recovery: autoscaler reduced queue depth to baseline within 40–90s after the burst decayed (depends on backend cold-starts).

Notes & recommended short-term mitigations:
1) Configure per-route burst window: allow 2x steady rate for 45s, then enforce token/sec taper to avoid long queue growth.
2) Add a circuit-breaker threshold on enqueue latency (e.g., >250ms) to return a synthetic 429 with Retry-After to the client — this reduces downstream cascades.
3) Tune autoscale cooldown to be slightly more aggressive for short bursts (reduce scale-down cooldown from 120s -> 60s).
4) For TTFT-sensitive endpoints, we recommend keeping a warm connection pool (pre-warmed GPUs) for critical routes.

Attached: burst_probe_results.csv (per-request sample, 28MB compressed) and a one-page draft SLO (slo_proposal.pdf).

I’ll upload the full logs to the MAP folder and link them in the HubSpot record after Olga signs off.

—Marcus
Performance Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP: performance validation checklist & burst-probe findings — next steps

Sam —

Appreciate the quick turn. The short summary: baseline met our provisional SLOs, but burst probes show TTFT and p95 degradation when queue depth grows beyond ~1.8k — we saw transient 429s and a small number of 503s.

Proposed next steps for the MAP:
- Immediate: accept Marcus’s mitigations as the MAP remediation tasks (rate-limit taper + enqueue-circuit-breaker + autoscale cooldown tweak). Owner: Redwood (Marcus & Rishi). Target: 12/03.
- Verification: run a follow-up 1-day verification with mitigation enabled 12/04–12/04 (single day) and produce an exec summary. Owner: Redwood.
- Acceptance: Acme devops to validate TTFT improvement on 12/07 verification run and sign technical acceptance. Owner: Acme.
- Contract decision: moveable to 12/10 if verification completes early; procurement copied here.

Sam, if you’re ok with the mitigations and owners, I’ll update the MAP spreadsheet and request an engineering readout on 12/02 to walk through the runbook. Once you confirm I’ll also add the SLO pdf into the MAP and push the HubSpot update.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Olga
